name: Single-Arm / Single-Leg Elevated Plank
description: The single-arm or single-leg plank removes one point of contact from the standard high plank, dramatically increasing the anti-rotation demand on the obliques and quadratus lumborum as the core resists the tendency to rotate toward the lifted limb. The contralateral variation — lifting one arm and the opposite leg simultaneously — maximises this anti-rotation challenge while also requiring lumbopelvic control in multiple planes. It is a highly effective progression from the standard plank without adding any external load.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard high plank position: hands under shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heel, core braced.
execution.setup_instructions: Master the standard high plank for 60+ seconds before attempting single-limb variations.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a high plank. Brace the core maximally.
Step 2: For single-arm variation: slowly lift one hand off the floor, extending the arm forward or placing it on the lower back.
Step 3: For contralateral variation: simultaneously lift one hand and the opposite foot off the floor.
Step 4: Hold the position without allowing the hips to rotate or drop.
Step 5: Return the limb(s) to the floor and repeat on the other side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe shallowly but continuously. Do not hold the breath during the hold.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips toward the lifted arm — the hips must remain perfectly square
Widening the support foot to compensate rather than maintaining proper challenge
safety_considerations: Regress immediately if hip rotation cannot be controlled
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Isometric hold for time — typically 20–40 seconds per side.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Hold for 20–40 seconds each side. Slow, controlled transitions.
coaching_cues: Hips square — a glass of water sits on your lower back and cannot spill
Squeeze the working glute and opposite shoulder
